question_1: Does H8 benefit from an independent first block when its shared and final blocks retain the same initialization?
question_2: How does a wider four-update shared trunk compare at approximately the same counted forward MACs?

C7B1.initialization: Reuse same-seed native H8 stem/head/shared S/final Z; replace its independent first A with S. In native B8 draw order, retain branch indices 1 and 2.

C4W45.initialization: Native C initialization at width 45; not tensor-matched to narrower models.
C4W45.width_selection: Minimize absolute MAC error to C8 width32 depth8 among integer widths 1 through 128 using recurrent_cnn.costs.mac_breakdown, before training.
C4W45.caveat: Native GroupNorm uses gcd(8,width): 1 group at width45 versus 8 at width32. This is a native depth/width trade-off, not an isolated depth intervention or an exact all-operation compute match.

recipe.pairing: Exact data/split/per-seed subset hashes must match the archived H8 run identities.

controls: Archived selected-validation B8, C8 and H8 runs; no retraining or official-test inference.

outcomes: train-validation gap at selected and final checkpoints
analysis.intervals: Nominal paired Student-t 95% intervals, df=4; exploratory, no multiplicity correction.
analysis.interpretation: C7B1 tests removing H8's separate first block with its other initial tensors held fixed. It alone cannot prove that the final block is the source of all H8 gains; a first-only control is not part of this request.

execution.isolation: One process and run directory per model/seed; all outputs/cache/temp paths in a fresh run-owned namespace; no test file staged; no input deletion or overwrite.
execution.guards: Short launcher proof before the full run; stop own process tree on timeout, no progress or insufficient free RAM.
